question:
I run DBT models, implemented as either materialized views or tables in Oracle data warehouse. The models are slow to SELECT from. To improve performance, what is the best practice for creating indexes in DBT models, if that model should run in Oracle (or even better, in database-agnostic way)?

I defined indexes on these data structures, by manually logging in the database. I wonder however whether there is a better way to do this. Optimally, these indexes should be defined at DBT level (in the DBT yaml file) rather than Oracle level. That way the configuration would be kept in one place, clean and manageable. The documentation isn't clear for me whether this can be done in a universal way or is this actually meant to be done on database level.
title: define index in DBT model in Oracle
answer:
I guess using post hook in config block you can create index. Can you please refer below link and try same for Oracle? Although the given query is for MS SQL server but I guess if you try in similar way it should work
